claim: Fedora 44 was released on 28 April 2026, continuing Fedora's roughly six-month release cadence.
quote: Fedora 44 release date is confirmed for April 28, 2026.

claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS was released 23 April 2026 with five years of security updates through April 2031.
quote: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS will receive security updates and critical bug fixes for five years.

claim: Fedora's default installer does not create a btrfs layout suited to snapshot management, and automatic pre/post snapshots require manually installing snapper plus the DNF5 actions plugin and grub-btrfs.
quote: Fedora's default installer is reliable, but it does not create a Btrfs layout suited for advanced snapshot management. Snapper is in the default Fedora repos, and you can install it along with the DNF5 actions plugin, which is needed for automatic pre/post snapshots.

claim: Bluefin checks for updates every six hours and applies them at reboot; the stable stream publishes weekly images with a kernel gated about two weeks behind Fedora; rollback uses bootc status / bootc switch to dated tags; local package layering is locked off by default via LockLayering and warned to require manual maintenance and longer updates.
quote: Bluefin checks for updates every six hours, applying them automatically at reboot. The stable stream (default) publishes weekly images... Enable local layering by setting LockLayering=false in /etc/rpm-ostreed.conf, though this requires manual maintenance and increases update times.

claim: Arch Linux posted roughly thirteen manual-intervention or breaking-change advisories between January 2025 and July 2026, including .NET packages (Dec 2025), NVIDIA 590 dropping Pascal (Dec 2025), linux-firmware (Jun 2025), varnish renamed to vinyl-cache (May 2026), plus an active malicious-AUR-package incident in June 2026.
quote: 2026-07-21: virtualbox-ext-vnc >= 7.2.12-2 requires manual intervention; 2026-06-12: Active AUR malicious packages incident; 2026-05-25: Breaking changes for all users of varnish, which is renamed to vinyl-cache; 2025-12-11: .NET packages may require manual intervention

claim: Debian 13 trixie ships nodejs 20.19.2.
quote: Package: nodejs (20.19.2+dfsg-1+deb13u2)

claim: Node.js 20 (Iron) reached end-of-life on 24 March 2026; the maintained LTS lines in mid-2026 are 22 and 24, with 26 as Current.
quote: v20 Iron — Maintenance LTS — First Released Apr 17, 2023 — EOL Mar 24, 2026

claim: Debian 13 trixie ships the Linux 6.12 series, GCC 14.2, Python 3.13, GNOME 48 and KDE Plasma 6.3.6.
quote: The distribution ships with the 6.12 series... GCC upgraded to version 14.2 (from 12.2)... Python 3.13... KDE Plasma 6.3.6 represents the first Debian release shipping Plasma 6

claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS ships the Linux 7.0 kernel for the latest hardware support.
quote: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Now Available & Powered By Linux 7.0

claim: openSUSE integrates snapper with btrfs as a first-class, default-enabled helper for reverting the system to a previous state.
quote: Snapper is deeply integrated with the Btrfs filesystem, serving as an easy to use helper for the built in functions of Btrfs.

claim: Every rpm-ostree operation is offline and composes a new deployment applied at reboot; the system keeps two bootable deployments and rpm-ostree rollback swaps the default; the docs state most software should go into a container and reserve layering for kernel modules and driver daemons.
quote: By default, every rpm-ostree operation is 'offline' - it has no effect on your running system, and will only take effect when you reboot... most software should go into a container

claim: A May 2026 Fedora Kinoite 44 thread shows an update blocked by an NVIDIA akmod dependency conflict during a kernel bump.
quote: kmod-nvidia-3:595.71.05-1.fc45.x86_64 requires akmod-nvidia = 3:595.71.05-1.fc45, but none of the providers can be installed

claim: openSUSE Tumbleweed publishes snapshots several times a week, gated by openQA testing; the update command is zypper dup, and rollback is done by booting a read-only snapshot from GRUB2 then running snapper rollback.
quote: Tumbleweed receives updates on a continuous basis, usually several times a week... Reboot and select 'Start Bootloader from a read-only snapshot' in GRUB2... run sudo snapper rollback

claim: In June 2026 the Fedora 43 to 44 upgrade silently failed on btrfs-subvolume layouts because the /system-update symlink was invisible to systemd; the workaround was dropping to a non-graphical target and using dnf-3 instead of dnf5.
quote: dnf-system-upgrade.service skipped, unmet condition check ConditionPathExists=/system-update

claim: Debian 13.6 was released on 11 July 2026 as a point release of the trixie stable series.
quote: Updated Debian 13: 13.6 released

claim: Each Fedora release is supported for about 13 months — until roughly one month after the release of version X+2 — allowing users to skip a release.
quote: Release X is supported until one month (4 weeks) after the release of Release X+2.

claim: From Leap 16.0 onward every minor release receives 24 months of maintenance, enabled by sharing a binary core with SUSE Linux Enterprise.
quote: Starting with Leap 16.0, every Minor Release receives maintenance and support for 24 months.

claim: openSUSE Leap 15 reached end of life in April 2026, closing a roughly eight-year era.
quote: Closing Out a Roughly 8-Year Era

claim: openSUSE Aeon targets 'lazy developers' with automated snapshot-based updates applied at reboot and uniquely automatic updates of the OS, Flatpaks and distroboxes, but ships almost no base software and is explicitly not for system tinkerers.
quote: System-tinkerers need not apply.

claim: Arch upgrades can fail on a stale signing keyring after long gaps; the fix is pacman -Sy --needed archlinux-keyring before pacman -Su, and a weekly systemd timer refreshes trusted key signatures.
quote: Since 2022-07-29, the archlinux-keyring-wkd-sync.service and associated systemd timer have been created and enabled by default, fetching new signatures of already trusted keys once a week

claim: Machines left un-updated for a long period hit interrupted pacman upgrades caused by out-of-date keyring packages.
quote: If you haven't run any updates/upgrades in a while, the update operation might be interrupted due to out of date Archlinux keyring libraries.

claim: NixOS is configured declaratively and every configuration change adds a boot-menu entry (a generation) that can be booted to roll back.
quote: The GRUB boot menu shows a list of available configurations, with every configuration change adding a new item to the menu, allowing you to easily roll back to a previous configuration if something goes wrong.

claim: nixos-rebuild creates new system generations; rolling back means selecting an older generation in the boot menu.
quote: To rollback to an old generation, simply select it in the boot menu and boot into it.

claim: Timeshift's btrfs mode only supports Ubuntu-style @ and @home subvolume layouts, so Fedora users are steered to the slower rsync mode.
quote: On Fedora, the recommendation is to use RSYNC mode, as TimeShift BTRFS mode only supports Ubuntu-style btrfs layouts with @ and @home subvolumes.

claim: Microsoft's official .NET packages failed to install on Debian trixie because their metadata declared libicu52 through libicu74 while trixie ships libicu76, making dotnet-sdk-9.0 uninstallable.
quote: The official Microsoft .NET packages declare dependencies for libicu versions 52 through 74, but Debian Trixie ships with libicu76.

claim: Ubuntu LTS releases freeze their kernel at release time, so hardware bought later may lack drivers; HWE kernels backport newer upstream kernels into the LTS to fix this.
quote: Ubuntu LTS releases ship with a kernel version frozen at release time. For hardware purchased after the LTS release date, the bundled kernel may lack support for newer components... Hardware Enablement (HWE) kernels solve this by bringing newer upstream kernels to LTS releases.

claim: Ubuntu LTS offers a GA kernel frozen at release and an HWE stack that provides newer kernel and display support on a rolling basis, with desktop installs defaulting to HWE.
quote: The Ubuntu LTS enablement, or Hardware Enablement (HWE), stack provides newer kernel and X11 display support for existing Ubuntu LTS releases.

claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS adds a virtualization HWE stack shipping newer QEMU, libvirt, EDK2 and SeaBIOS via -hwe packages, refreshed every six months during the first two years of the LTS.
quote: Future Ubuntu 26.04 LTS point releases will ship with updated versions of QEMU, libvirt, EDK2, and SeaBIOS via new '-hwe' post-fixed packages.

claim: Bazzite, a Fedora Atomic based image, reached about 5.53% share among Linux Steam users in late 2025 while Linux overall hit an all-time-high 3.2% of Steam users in 2026.
quote: Bazzite grew 1.29% to 5.53% market share in November 2025... Linux reached 3.2% of all Steam users as reported in the 2026 Steam Hardware Survey

claim: Toolbx is the Red Hat project preinstalled on Fedora Atomic desktops; Distrobox is the community superset that will run any container image as a dev environment.
quote: In 2026, the honest summary is that Toolbx is what's already on your Fedora atomic desktop and it works, while Distrobox is what you reach for the moment that's not enough. Distrobox is, by any honest measure, a near-superset of Toolbx today.

claim: Using IDEs inside toolbox/distrobox on atomic desktops creates friction at the container boundary — for example needing workarounds to launch a host browser for VS Code's GitHub sign-in — leading the author to switch to Neovim, which installs cleanly inside the container.
quote: if you use VSCode and want to authenticated with GitHub to pull your settings, you might need to do a couple of workarounds to get a firefox or any other browser inside the container to launch it

claim: Fedora Silverblue preinstalls Podman rather than Docker, and dnf cannot be used to install packages directly on the host.
quote: The base OS is managed by rpm-ostree, and you cannot use dnf to install packages directly on the host.

claim: Bluefin DX bakes Docker Engine (default for VS Code devcontainers), Podman, Incus, KVM/QEMU with virt-manager, VS Code with the Remote-Containers extension and Homebrew into the image, activated with ujust devmode plus ujust dx-group.
quote: unlike traditional Linux distributions where development tools are installed directly on the host system, bluefin-dx implements a container-first architecture where development happens in isolated environments

claim: Bluefin positions itself as not a distribution, with the user's relationship being with Flathub, Homebrew and their own containers rather than a host package manager.
quote: Your relationship is with Flathub, homebrew, and whatever you put in your containers.

claim: Flathub recorded more than 435 million downloads in 2025, a 21% year-over-year increase and over fifteen times its 2020 volume, across more than 2,800 apps.
quote: more than 435 million total downloads during the year, representing a 21% increase from 2024's 360.4 million

claim: CachyOS, an Arch-based rolling release, took the number one DistroWatch position in mid-2025 and held it for over eighteen consecutive months.
quote: CachyOS has topped DistroWatch rankings for 18+ months straight, the longest sustained run at #1 in recent history.

claim: CachyOS is an Arch Linux based rolling-release distribution focused on performance tuning, with a graphical installer and a Handheld Edition.
quote: CachyOS is an Arch Linux–based, rolling‑release distribution that emerged with a clear focus on performance.
